label: z fed back as 1st/2nd copied token
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the input token is z and it is one of the first two copied tokens fed back: input at step L+1 (original token 0 = z, recall_idx 1) or step L+2 (original token 1 = z, recall_idx 2). Magnitude is strongly modulated by position. When z is the first original token, the feature fires at about 0.85-1.0 of max (that case holds about 82% of the mass). When z is the second original token, it fires weakly, about 0.2-0.4 of max. It never fires during the original phase or at the delimiter, never on any non-z input, and never on z at later copy positions. False positives (about 4.5%) are mostly short sequences (L=3-4) where z is the second original token at recall_idx 2.

issues: Main claims hold on the test split. Precision is 0.959, recall 0.9998, mass recall 0.99999. On dev the feature fires on no non-z input; it fires once in the original phase and never at the delimiter. The 5 test misses are tiny (about 0.02-0.03 of max) and hold 0.0% of the mass.

Magnitude split confirmed. z at recall_idx 1 has precision 1.0, holds 81.8% of the mass and fills the top two activation quartiles. z at recall_idx 2 holds 18.2% and sits only in the bottom two quartiles.

The false positives form a clear, systematic group. Almost all are z at recall_idx 2 with L<=4 (2788 predicted, precision 0.51). With L==3 (to_go 0) it essentially never fires (precision 0.007, 421 cases). With L==4 it fires about 60% of the time. With L>=5 precision is 0.9999. The explanation does mention this short-sequence group, but 'mostly L=3-4' undersells it: for L=3 the 2nd-copied-token case is a hard zero.
The label slightly overclaims: 'z fed back as 2nd copied token' does not hold when L=3, and only holds partly when L=4.
skeptic.revised_label: z fed back as 1st copied token (strong) or 2nd copied token (weak; not when L=3)
